A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DND work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, relocated and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen3 benchmark results, architectural and training ablations, and token-selection analyses in Tables 1–2 and the main-text and appendix figures.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Llama and Gemma evaluations, an ITT comparison, measured inference throughput, and entropy and hidden-state analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same token-choice routing, same-layer nested processing, normalized fusion, router losses, buffer proportional control and EMA synchronization. Applying DND to additional backbones introduces no documented change to its procedure.

E1.justification: The described SFT data sources and benchmark suite are unchanged. v2 Table 1 uses the eleven tasks already evaluated in v1 Table 2; the added backbones, throughput measurements and diagnostics expand configurations and evaluation procedures rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds ITT as an evaluated comparator for Qwen3-1.7B, whereas v1 only discussed ITT in related work. This is a targeted addition to one model's comparison; the original comparators remain, and MOR is still compared descriptively rather than through reported benchmark results.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama-3.2-1B and Gemma3-1B configurations and a reportedly compute-matched ITT comparison. It also introduces throughput testing across four input/decode-length combinations on one H100 with a single batch, plus entropy and hidden-state diagnostic measurements. These substantially expand the evaluation design without revising the retained Qwen protocols.

E4.justification: New Figure 4 tests whether frequently selected tokens have higher original logit entropy and larger entropy reductions after DND. New Appendix D and Figure 8 examine selection against hidden-state changes. These add substantive tests of the selection mechanism; the original ablations, control analyses and qualitative examples remain.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 4 newly reports fitted linear trends and Pearson correlations, adding statistical estimation to the diagnostic analyses. Appendix B retains the same 16 inferences per AIME question; neither additional run counts nor new benchmark confidence intervals are reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds Llama average scores of 45.37 versus 47.98 with DND, Gemma scores of 47.08 versus 49.58, and an ITT score of 59.58 against Qwen DND's retained 61.41. Table 3 newly reports DND throughput at 91.6–93.1% of vanilla speed. New diagnostic findings include Pearson correlations of 0.3359 and -0.5831. The original Qwen benchmark and ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10) and Appendix A's computational assumptions and FLOPs derivation, including the 6.27% overhead estimate, are unchanged. The new diagnostic plots introduce empirical measurements and fitted relationships, not new formal definitions, theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion extend explicit validation claims to Llama3.2-1B and Gemma3-1B, including their reported 2.61- and 2.50-point gains. The central contributions concerning selective nested computation, routing control and post-training integration remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets entropy and hidden-state findings as evidence that DND revisits uncertain tokens and improves their representations. It also attributes ITT's limited gains to routing-related training/inference mismatch and emphasizes complementary router and threshold controls. These refine the mechanism discussion; the limitations are retained, moving from Appendix E to F.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly discloses that all parameters are trainable with the same learning rate; v1 did not specify this. Appendix B adds two-epoch, 64-H100, approximately 1–2-day training details for Llama and Gemma, while Table 3 supplies BF16 and vLLM-kernel information. Existing Qwen settings and the promised future code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and the expanded MOR comparison table distinguish MOR's parameter-efficiency objective from DND's enhancement of existing pretrained models, adding discussion of from-scratch training costs. v2 also adds Ma et al. (2025), Estimating LLM Uncertainty with Evidence, to support the entropy interpretation. The broader related-work positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the MOR discussion and ablation interpretation, organizes main results into base, scaling and throughput discussions, and inserts an appendix subsection for token-selection analysis. Most introductory and methodological prose remains unchanged, so this is a limited narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: v2 adds a consolidated dense-model performance table, a throughput table, two entropy scatterplots and a hidden-state violin plot. It also expands the MOR table with a Purpose row and relocates retained displays and appendix material. This substantially expands the visual evidence beyond simple renumbering or numerical cell updates.

improvement.justification: v1's efficacy evidence was confined to Qwen models and its overhead assessment was analytical. v2's Llama/Gemma results, direct ITT comparison and measured throughput address important gaps in generalizability, comparative effectiveness and practical cost. The new diagnostics also strengthen evidence about token selection, although correlations and lower entropy do not prove better representations as the text suggests. The broader empirical support provides a substantial overall improvement despite that interpretive overstatement.
